lens: A1 = Own-Policy-Adherence: Naming. Authoritative corpus consulted: ADR-0056 (Rust Clean Architecture BNF v4.1 — flat microservice grammar + 12-layer enum, amended to 13-layer per ADR-0105), ADR-0242 (oyatie-is-a-tenant doctrine, reserved-namespace family), ADR-0244 (tenant as universal scoping primitive, dotted hierarchical sub-scope, manifest schema), ADR-0246 (policy-engine substrate promotion, 47-crate redistribution), ADR-0263 (observability emission contract, metric naming `oya:<microservice>:<bc>:<metric>_<unit>:<type>`, log schema layer enumeration), ADR-0284 (platform-owner-name indirection, single named constant). Memory anchor: feedback_naming_justification (2026-05-13) — 'Every new name must carry one-line justification proving v4 BNF + 12-layer-enum conformance at scaffold time.'
summary: BNF v4.1 grammar + 13-layer enum mechanics are correctly applied where they ARE applied: the ADR-0246 47-crate redistribution parses cleanly, the `oya-check-*` flat namespace is used consistently for the ~17 new CI lanes, the `oya-shared-platform-constants-kernel` indirection crate is BNF-clean, reserved-namespace defence-in-depth (Cedar fragment + Rust admission gate + Unicode TR#39 normalisation) is comprehensive, and migration/Cedar/Postgres file naming conventions are internally consistent across all five ADRs. Four structural defects block A1 PASS: (1) ADR-0263 §D-6 invents four log-schema `layer` values (`tool`, `mock`, `fixture`, `bench`) that are NOT in the ADR-0105 13-value canonical enum and simultaneously drops four canonical values (`infrastructure`, `cli`, `grpc`, `graphql`) from the same enumeration — silent parallel-vocabulary fork inside a keystone whose explicit purpose is to lock naming down; (2) NONE of the five keystone ADRs carries the `## Naming justification` table mandated by feedback_naming_justification, despite collectively introducing ~100 new names — and the doctrinal irony is that ADR-0284 cites `feedback_naming_justification` in its `related_memory` block while itself omitting the table; (3) ADR-0244 §D-2 sub-scope segment regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` contradicts the reserved-segment list two paragraphs later (regex forbids `_`; reserved list requires leading `_`) — schema cannot be implemented as written; (4) ADR-0246 §Implementation surface omits the `[workspace.metadata.oya.microservices.policy-engine]` registry insertion that ADR-0056 §'Microservice registry' makes a BNF-validation prerequisite for every `oya-policy-engine-*` crate. Additional minor: manifest-`tier` enum in ADR-0244 §D-5 reuses the lexeme `kernel`, lexically colliding with layer-enum `kernel`; reserved-namespace coverage stops at tenant slug + sub-scope and does not extend to other tenant-writable identifier surfaces (Cedar action names, audit-stream names, FinOps cost-centers, Kafka topics, K8s namespaces).

per_adr_findings.scope_summary: Reserved-namespace doctrine (tenant slug `oyatie` + 4-root family + UTS#39 normalisation), sub-scope conventions, 3 CI lanes, 13 implementation-surface artifacts.
passes: Reserved-namespace family (`oyatie`, `oya`, `oyat`, `oyati`) + prefix-with-separator + IDN-homograph defence per TR#36 is the most rigorous reserved-identifier doctrine in the corpus.

File names follow conventions: `microservices/tenancy/src/reserved_namespace.rs` (Rust snake_case module convention); Cedar fragment `policy-engine/fragments/reserved-tenant-namespace.cedar` (kebab + dot-extension).
Sub-scope syntax `<tenant_id>.<segment-1>.<segment-2>` (dotted-path; max 4-5 levels) matches AWS IAM principal-path hierarchical pattern cited in §D-2.
defects: No `## Naming justification` table present despite ~10 new names introduced (tenant slug, reserved roots, 3 CI lanes, 8 implementation-surface file paths, audit-stream name family `oyatie.{root,foundry,security,finance,platform-ops}`, sub-scope examples like `oyatie.foundry.ci-agent`). Memory anchor `feedback_naming_justification` is unsatisfied.

per_adr_findings.scope_summary: Universal tenant-scoping primitive — tenant ID regex, dotted hierarchical sub-scope, canonical tenants table DDL (~30 columns, 8 Postgres ENUM types), Cedar entity-types, manifest schema replacing ADR-0221 §M-04.
passes: Tenant ID regex `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}(\.[a-z0-9-]{1,62}){0,4}$` is well-specified, RFC 1035 DNS-label compatible per segment, NFKC-normalised at admission.
Customer-tenant prefix convention (`tenant-*`, `partner-*`, `reseller-*`, `b2c-*`) gives orthographic distinction from platform-owner slug at one glance in any log.

Postgres ENUM types (`audience_type`, `merchant_status`, `payout_method`, `tenant_lifecycle_state`, `dr_pair_strategy`, `bootstrap_tier`) use snake_case (Postgres convention); ENUM variants UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; CHECK-constraint regexes are anchored; COMMENT ON TABLE statements present — schema-naming hygiene is strong.
Cedar entity-types `Tenancy::Tenant`, `Tenancy::SubScope`, `Tenancy::Principal`, `Tenancy::CrossTenantGrant`, `Tenancy::Resource` follow Cedar v4.2 namespace convention.
defects: MAJOR: §D-2 sub-scope segment regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` contradicts the reserved-segment list (`_system`, `_bootstrap`, `_migration`, `_audit`, `_observability`, `_policy`, `_admin`, `_root`) two paragraphs below — underscore is not in the regex character class. Schema cannot be implemented as written. The §D-3 `tenant_sub_scopes.sub_scope_path` CHECK constraint inherits the same contradiction.

MINOR: §D-5 manifest `tier` enum `[substrate, kernel, product, studio, marketplace, edge]` reuses the lexeme `kernel`, colliding with the layer-enum `kernel`. Same word, different concept (tier-position vs layer-position). Onboarding-confusion + grep-ambiguity risk.
No `## Naming justification` table despite ~30 new names introduced (regex literal, 8 Postgres ENUMs with ~40 variants, 5 Cedar entity-types, manifest-schema field set, 2+ CI lanes).

per_adr_findings.scope_summary: Promotes `cedar-fragment-coverage` BC out of Ontology into peer substrate µservice `microservices/policy-engine/`; 8 bounded contexts; 47-crate redistribution (5 renamed + 42 new); 10 gRPC operations; per-cell deployment topology.
passes: 47-crate matrix in §D-3 is BNF v4.1 + 13-layer-enum compliant. Every crate matches `^oya-<microservice>-<bc-tokens>-<layer>$` with microservice = `policy-engine` (2 kebab tokens, within ADR-0056 1..3 cap) and layer ∈ {kernel, domain, usecase, api, adapter, rest, worker, sdk, app}.

Shared SDK crates `oya-shared-policy-engine-client-{kernel,adapter,sdk}` use the canonical `shared` slot2 per ADR-0056 §'Microservice registry' (`shared` is reserved for cross-µservice SDK / utility crates) and target `kernel`/`adapter`/`sdk` layers (correct: SDK depends only on kernel per ADR-0056 §'sdk-kernel-only' lane).

Per-µservice flat directory layout (`PRD.md`, `api/`, `capabilities/`, `calls.yaml`, `fragments/`, `iac/helm/`, `migrations/`, `slos/`, `src/`, `tests/`) matches ADR-0131 per-microservice flat layout doctrine.
Migration file naming `0001_fragment_registry_init.sql` through `0005_genesis_fragment_seed.sql` matches `^[0-9]{4}_[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.sql$` per-µservice counter convention.

Renamed crates from `oya-ontology-cedar-fragment-coverage-*` → `oya-policy-engine-fragment-registry-*` correctly migrate slot2 from `ontology` to `policy-engine` and rename the BC from `cedar-fragment-coverage` to `fragment-registry` (4 kebab → 2 kebab; cleaner, still semantically clear).
defects: MAJOR: §Implementation surface omits the `[workspace.metadata.oya.microservices.policy-engine]` registry insertion. ADR-0056 §'Microservice registry' validates slot2 against the workspace metadata; without the row, every `oya-policy-engine-*` crate fails the `oya-shared-architecture-check-cli -- lib-name-parity` lane on first build. Slot2 registry add is a 0-ADR action, but a keystone ADR introducing 47 crates of a new µservice MUST exhibit the diff for auditability.

MINOR: 8 new BCs (`fragment-registry` rename + 7 new: `evaluator`, `signing-chain`, `hot-reload`, `coverage-audit`, `pack-overlay`, `tenant-overlay`, `bootstrap-genesis`) require BC-registry update at `docs/standards/bounded-contexts.md` (ADR-0056 §'Bounded Context Registry as a Living Document' — 0-ADR action). Not exhibited in §Implementation surface.

INFO: BC `bootstrap-genesis` ships only 4 crates with crate-name BC slot truncated to `bootstrap` (e.g., `oya-policy-engine-bootstrap-kernel`) rather than `bootstrap-genesis`. BNF-legal (multi-token vs single-token BC tokens are both permitted) but the BC-name-vs-crate-name-slot mismatch should be justified in a naming-justification row.
No `## Naming justification` table despite 47 new crates + 8 BCs + 10 gRPC operations + 9 Helm template names + 5 migration files + 5 SLO files.

per_adr_findings.scope_summary: Tier-1 observability emission contract — Three Pillars (metrics + logs + traces), W3C Trace Context propagation, mandatory `tenant_id` label, structured JSON log schema `oyatie/log/v1`, metric naming `oya:<microservice>:<bc>:<metric>_<unit>:<type>`, exemplars, audit-chain linkage, PII scrubbing, schema versioning.
passes: Three Pillars contract (metrics + logs + traces unified via correlation IDs) is grounded in Charity Majors / Cindy Sridharan canonical observability doctrine.
Mandatory `tenant_id` label across all three pillars is consistent with ADR-0242 universal-tenant doctrine.

OpenTelemetry semantic-convention attribute keys (`oyatie.tenant.id`, `oyatie.tenant.subscope`, `oyatie.audit.event_id`, `oyatie.slo.touched`, `oyatie.endpoint.is_new`, `oyatie.latency.bucket`) use the OTel-canonical `<namespace>.<concept>.<attribute>` dotted form with `oyatie` as the namespace prefix — well-formed.
Reserved key prefixes (`oyatie.*` platform-owned; `tenant.*` tenant-supplied; `_internal.*` substrate-internal) cleanly partition the attribute namespace.
Schema-version literal `oyatie/log/v1` follows the `<namespace>/<artifact>/v<n>` convention common in OpenAPI + JSON Schema ecosystems.
defects: MAJOR: §D-6 log-schema mandatory-field table cites 'One of the 13 layers per ADR-0105 (`kernel`, `domain`, `usecase`, `api`, `adapter`, `rest`, `worker`, `sdk`, `app`, `tool`, `mock`, `fixture`, `bench`)' — but ADR-0105's actual canonical enum (verified against ADR-0056 §'12-Value Layer Enum' as amended) is `{kernel, domain, application/usecase, app, adapter, infrastructure, cli, rest, grpc, graphql, worker, sdk, api}`. ADR-0263 invents 4 values (`tool`, `mock`, `fixture`, `bench`) AND silently drops 4 canonical values (`infrastructure`, `cli`, `grpc`, `graphql`) from what it labels 'the 13 layers.' This is a silent parallel-vocabulary fork inside a keystone bundle whose explicit purpose is to lock naming down. ADR-0056 §'12-Value Layer Enum' is explicit: 'Adding a layer value is a 1-ADR action. No aliases or overlaps.' ADR-0263 is doing exactly that without amending ADR-0105.

MINOR: §D-7 metric naming `oya:<microservice>:<bc>:<metric>_<unit>:<type>` uses colon as separator. Prometheus exposition format accepts colons syntactically (regex `[a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_:]*`) but convention reserves colons for recording-rule outputs; raw instrumented metrics typically use underscores. Mimir + Prometheus 2.x ingestion will accept but OSS dashboards / promql linters / external tooling may flag. Source-driven-development confirmation against current Prometheus naming spec recommended.

No `## Naming justification` table despite 7 CI lanes + 7-crate shared-observability-client family + ~30 metric naming examples + 3 backend-qualified adapter crates + schema-version literal + metric-prefix `oya:` + W3C-protocol-header-key prohibitions.

per_adr_findings.scope_summary: Platform-owner-name indirection — single named constant `PLATFORM_OWNER_TENANT_SLUG`, spec file `/specs/platform-constants.json`, generated crate `oya-shared-platform-constants-kernel`, brand-vs-slug separation, rebrand migration procedure.
passes: Constant name `PLATFORM_OWNER_TENANT_SLUG` is SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (Rust compile-time const convention).

Generated crate name `oya-shared-platform-constants-kernel` matches BNF v4.1: slot2 = `shared` (cross-µservice utility crate per ADR-0056); BC tokens = `platform-constants` (2 kebab tokens, semantically clear); layer = `kernel` (correct — a constant module with zero I/O lives in `kernel` per ADR-0056 layer semantics).
Spec file path `/specs/platform-constants.json` follows the flat-spec convention established in ADR-0119.
Helper functions `dsar_contact_email()`, `principal_prefix()`, `is_platform_owner_slug()` use snake_case + predicate-style naming (Rust idiom).

Brand-vs-slug separation matches Apple Intelligence pattern (slug stable, internal; brand i18n'd, marketing-controlled). Per-product brand keys (`product-mail-display-name` etc) in Fluent are kebab-case (Fluent convention).

CI lanes (`oya-check-no-hardcoded-platform-owner-slug`, `oya-check-platform-owner-constant-indirection`, `oya-check-platform-owner-brand-vs-slug-separation`, `oya-check-platform-constants-codegen-clean`) follow `oya-check-<rule-name>` flat namespace per ADR-0056 §'Check-namespace exemption'.
Cedar template extension `.cedar.tera` (vs final artifact `.cedar`) cleanly distinguishes pre-substitution from signed artifact — template-vs-artifact naming clarity.
defects: MAJOR (doctrinal irony): ADR-0284 cites `feedback_naming_justification` in `related_memory` but does NOT carry a `## Naming justification` table itself. The ADR introduces 5 platform constants + 1 spec file + 1 shared crate + 4 CI lanes + 5 Fluent message keys + 2 codegen tool names. The exact memory the ADR references requires the table; the ADR omits it.

INFO: Codegen tool names `oya-codegen-platform-constants`, `oya-codegen-cedar-fragments` use the `oya-codegen-*` family but this family is not registered in ADR-0056 alongside the `oya-check-*` flat namespace. Either (a) `oya-codegen-*` should be added as a sibling flat namespace by ADR amendment, or (b) the tools should follow BNF (`oya-tooling-codegen-platform-constants-cli` etc.). Worth a one-line justification.

bnf_violations.violation: ADR-0263 claims to enumerate 'the 13 layers per ADR-0105' but lists a fork-set: invents `tool`, `mock`, `fixture`, `bench` (NOT in ADR-0105) and drops `infrastructure`, `cli`, `grpc`, `graphql` (which ARE in ADR-0105 per ADR-0056 §'12-Value Layer Enum'). This is a silent parallel-vocabulary fork.
bnf_violations.policy_anchor: ADR-0056 §'12-Value Layer Enum (closed)' — 'Adding a layer value is a 1-ADR action. No aliases or overlaps.'
bnf_violations.fix: Either (a) restrict `layer` to the actual ADR-0105 enum and drop tool/mock/fixture/bench (test-only emissions can carry a separate optional `emission_class ∈ {production, test, benchmark, fixture}` field), or (b) explicitly amend ADR-0105 inline in ADR-0263 §D-6 with an 'Amendment — extend layer enum' subsection. Recommendation: (a) — smaller blast radius; ADR-0105 stays semantically tight; test/bench/fixture are an orthogonal concern from architectural layer.

what_works: ADR-0242 §D-1 + §D-6 reserved-namespace family (`oyatie`, `oya`, `oyat`, `oyati` + prefix family `oyatie-*`/`oyatie.*`/`oyatie_*`) is comprehensive at the tenant-slug layer.

UTS#39 Unicode Security Mechanisms + NFKC normalisation + diacritic-strip + IDN-homograph defence per TR#36 — fully cited; implementation surface (`microservices/tenancy/src/reserved_namespace.rs`) follows.
Cedar fragment `policy-engine/fragments/reserved-tenant-namespace.cedar` enforces the reservation as a forbid rule at admission.

ADR-0284 §D-5 transitions the reserved list into a versioned constant (`PLATFORM_OWNER_RESERVED_NAMESPACE_ROOTS`) and codifies post-rebrand retention (legacy roots stay reserved indefinitely, preventing reclamation by a third party).

ADR-0244 §D-2 reserved sub-scope segments (`_system`, `_bootstrap`, `_migration`, `_audit`, `_observability`, `_policy`, `_admin`, `_root`) cover platform-internal sub-scope use cases (subject to the BNF-V02 regex resolution).
Verification checklist in ADR-0242 §Verification includes Cyrillic-confusable test (`is_reserved("оyatie") == Reserved`) — concrete test fixture for TR#39 implementation.
reserved_namespace_assessment.gap: Reserved-namespace coverage stops at the tenant + sub-scope layer. The keystone bundle does NOT reserve any of these tenant-writable identifier surfaces: (a) Cedar action namespaces — could a tenant author a Cedar action `oyatie::TombstoneTenant`?; (b) audit-stream names — a tenant might attempt to publish to a stream named `oyatie.root` if the audit-chain provisioner doesn't filter; (c) FinOps cost-center IDs — could collide with `oyatie-platform`; (d) sovereign-cloud pack IDs — could a tenant request pack name `oyatie-eu`?; (e) Kafka topic names — `policy-engine.fragment-reload.v1` is not in any reserved-topic policy; (f) ClickHouse per-tenant table prefixes; (g) Helm chart names; (h) Kubernetes namespaces; (i) container registry repo names. ADR-0242 reserves the tenant slug; a keystone-wide reserved-namespace doctrine should extend to every identifier surface a tenant can write to.
reserved_namespace_assessment.fix: Extend ADR-0284 §D-5 OR file ADR-0285 'Global reserved-identifier policy' declaring: 'Identifiers under any platform-managed surface that begin with `PLATFORM_OWNER_TENANT_SLUG` (after UTS #39 normalisation) are reserved.' Enumerate surfaces: tenant slug, sub-scope segment, Cedar action namespace, audit-stream name, FinOps cost-center ID, sovereign-cloud pack ID, Kafka topic name, ClickHouse table prefix, Helm chart name, K8s namespace, container registry repo name.

ambiguity_risks.quote: `layer` | string | One of the 13 layers per ADR-0105 (`kernel`, `domain`, `usecase`, `api`, `adapter`, `rest`, `worker`, `sdk`, `app`, `tool`, `mock`, `fixture`, `bench`)
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_a: ADR-0105 has been amended to include these 13 values and ADR-0263 is just stating it.
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_b: ADR-0263 is the amendment itself (1-ADR-action per ADR-0056) and ADR-0105 is extended in place by ADR-0263.
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_c: ADR-0263 misquotes ADR-0105 (likely reading given ADR-0105 + ADR-0056 §'12-Value Layer Enum' do not contain tool/mock/fixture/bench).
ambiguity_risks.downstream_risk: Lane `oya-check-log-schema-conformance` must implement one of these. If (a) or (b), it accepts emissions containing `layer: tool`. If (c), it rejects them. Pre-flight ambiguity = silent rejection or silent acceptance in production.

ambiguity_risks.location: ADR-0244 §D-2 sub-scope segment regex vs reserved list
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_a: Reserved segments are stored in a separate non-tenant-author table and bypass the segment regex.
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_b: Both lists were authored independently and conflict; the regex is the implemented gate; the reserved list is documentation only.
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_c: Both lists are authoritative; the regex must permit underscore. The reserved-list authors will discover the conflict at implementation time.
ambiguity_risks.downstream_risk: Engineers implementing `tenant_sub_scopes.sub_scope_path` CHECK constraint will pick one interpretation without coordinating. Schema drift between Cedar gate, Postgres CHECK, and admission-gate Rust code.

multi_perspective_assessment.executor_lens: 47 new crates land cleanly under BNF v4.1. CI lane `oya-shared-architecture-check-cli -- lib-name-parity` will pass IF the registry row from BNF-V03 is added; otherwise every PR scaffold fails day-1. The naming-justification gap is doctrinal noncompliance but not a build-breaker. ADR-0244 regex/reserved-list contradiction (BNF-V02) will surface at first schema-migration execution.
multi_perspective_assessment.stakeholder_lens: Substrate promotion is well-named; doctrine reads cleanly to a senior engineer. The layer-enum drift in ADR-0263 (BNF-V01) and the manifest-`tier`-vs-layer-`kernel` collision (BNF-V04) will confuse onboarding contributors and AI agents reading the corpus. Both fixes are 30 minutes of editing.
multi_perspective_assessment.skeptic_lens: Five keystone ADRs introducing ~177 names while skipping the naming-justification policy on the exact session that authored said policy is the kind of self-exception that compounds. The keystone is in fact the FIRST place the policy should land; landing without it is the worst-case violation. The reserved-namespace gap shows the doctrine stopped one logical step short — it locked the tenant slug but left every other tenant-writable identifier surface (Cedar action namespaces, audit streams, Kafka topics, K8s namespaces, etc.) unreserved. A future incident will exploit that gap. Recommend cross-facet alignment with A3-Structure + A4-Architecture reviewers on whether ADR-0285 'Global reserved-identifier policy + keystone-bundle naming registry' should land as a 15th keystone before bundle merges.

open_questions: Should the bundle file a shared ADR-0285 'Keystone-bundle naming registry' that the 14 keystones cite, rather than 14 separate `## Naming justification` sections? The 177-row table in one place may be more navigable + auditable than 14 fragments.

ADR-0263 §D-6 invented layer values (tool/mock/fixture/bench) suggest a missing concept (`emission_class` for test/bench code). Should §D-6 introduce that field explicitly, or should ADR-0105 amend to add the four values? Recommendation favours the former; cross-facet consensus required.

ADR-0244 manifest-`tier` enum collides lexically with layer-enum `kernel`. Should ADR-0245 (the source of the tier vocabulary) rename, or should the manifest schema rename, or both? Recommendation: ADR-0245 renames substrate-tier `kernel` → `substrate-core` and ADR-0244 inherits.
Should reserved-namespace coverage extend to non-tenant-writable surfaces (Helm chart name, K8s namespace, container registry repo)? Or is the scope correctly tenant-writable-only?
ADR-0263 §D-7 colon-form metric naming: confirm via current Prometheus naming spec whether colons in raw metric names are accepted by Mimir + Prometheus 2.x + OpenMetrics 1.0.0 linters.
verdict_justification: Four MAJOR findings block A1 PASS: (BNF-V01) silent layer-enum fork in ADR-0263 §D-6; (BNF-V02) self-contradicting sub-scope regex + reserved-list in ADR-0244 §D-2 (schema unimplementable as written); (BNF-V03) missing µservice-registry diff in ADR-0246 (47 crates will fail BNF validation day-1); (naming-justification absent) policy non-compliance across all 5 keystone ADRs, ~177 names introduced without a single justification row, in the very session that wrote the policy. Two MINOR findings (lexeme collision `tier::kernel` vs layer `kernel`; reserved-namespace coverage gap beyond tenant slug) compound the picture. The PASS observations (A1-PASS-01..07) show the BNF + 13-layer-enum mechanics are correctly applied where they ARE applied — the failures are policy-completeness rather than policy-correctness. Verdict: REVISE with fixes itemised per finding. Re-review on r2 with the naming-justification tables in place, the ADR-0263 layer-enum reconciled, the ADR-0244 §D-2 regex/reserved-list conflict resolved, and the ADR-0246 µservice-registry diff exhibited.

overall_signal_for_synthesizer.primary_signal: BNF v4.1 mechanics PASS where applied; policy-completeness fails across the bundle. Four BLOCKER fixes (layer-enum, sub-scope regex, µservice-registry, naming-justification) are 1-2 hours of editing collectively. Two MAJOR fixes (tier-rename, reserved-namespace extension) require cross-ADR coordination (ADR-0245, possibly new ADR-0285). Bundle should not merge without these.
overall_signal_for_synthesizer.synthesis_input_for_other_facets: A1 review confirms structural correctness of crate names + CI-lane names + reserved-namespace mechanics, but flags two doctrinal gaps that A3-Structure and A4-Architecture reviewers should cross-check: (1) the ADR-0105 layer-enum fork in ADR-0263 §D-6 — A3/A4 should verify the canonical 13-layer enum is the same one they assumed; (2) the missing µservice-registry diff in ADR-0246 — A3/A4 should check whether the bundle ships the registry row as a side-effect of another ADR or whether the gap is real. A1 also flags one cross-cutting policy gap (reserved-namespace coverage beyond tenant slug) that F-family facets (F1-correctness, F7-supply-chain, F13-compliance) may want to weigh.
